title: The Entire Market Relies On These Stocks
creator: Joseph Carlson After Hours
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Joseph Carlson frames Q3 earnings season as unusually consequential: S&P 500 earnings growth is expected above 35%, with the bulk driven by a small set of AI and energy companies, while bond yields rise and the index sits near highs — so the rally needs confirmation. He previews this week's reporters in depth. ASML (reporting Wednesday, his fifth-largest position at ~$124k) is expected to grow revenue 50–55% and EPS ~89%; despite a 33x forward P/E he holds into earnings, arguing ASML is a true monopoly whose high-NA EUV, supplier, customer and installed-base moats are widening. TSM shares the same top-of-the-food-chain bull case at a cheaper 21x forward P/E, and he sees no reason to sell. On JPMorgan he is positive into earnings but no longer holds it; on UnitedHealth he is staying out over business-model and regulatory dislike; Domino's he views coolly as DoorDash erodes its delivery edge. He then covers Meta's Muse Wonder launch — benchmark parity with Claude Opus, a personalised-agent advantage, and a stock he still calls undervalued — before a 'fail of the week' segment criticising Kelly Clarkson's viral post against a small Brooklyn business as disproportionate. Calls: ASML HOLD, TSM HOLD, META HOLD, UNH AVOID; JPM and DPZ mentioned without explicit calls.

calls.bear_case: Expectations are extreme this quarter; a miss would hurt the stock badly and the market has sold ASML down incorrectly before.
